observation: Overall layout: the original renders with almost no styling. It is a single column, left-aligned and full-width at 1440px, with stacked block flow and no flex or grid. The AI-built page is a styled magazine layout in a centred column about 1128px wide (156px side margins), built with flex (25 elements) and grid (5 elements).
Page length and text volume: the original is about 16,632px tall with about 1,049 words. The AI-built page is about 2,377px tall with about 332 words.

Spacing and alignment: the original's indentation is inconsistent, with lists and images at x=8, 48 or 88 from browser-default list padding. The AI-built page uses regular spacing: about 20px card gutters, 16px card padding and 40–60px between sections.

Typefaces: the original uses one serif, Andada, on about 1,325 elements. The AI-built page pairs Georgia serif (218 elements, used for headlines, quote and bio) with a system-ui sans (148 elements, used for nav, meta, labels, buttons and footer).

Body text: both pages set body text at 16px. The original uses mid-grey rgb(96,96,96) with line-height 'normal' and near-black links rgb(27,27,27). The AI-built page uses near-black rgb(29,29,31) with line-height 24.8px and grey rgb(107,107,112) for meta text.
Neither page has an h1, and post titles are h3 on both.

Heading structure: the original has 12 h2 section labels (College and University, Educations, Science, Latest Posts, footer widgets) and 50 h3s. The AI-built page has a single h2 ('BROWSE ARTICLES') and 26 h3s, which also cover category labels and the author name, plus h4 footer column titles.
Section h2 styling: the original's h2s are 24px bold grey serif labels with no rule. The AI-built h2 is a 14px bold, uppercase, letter-spaced label with a solid dark rule underneath.

Type hierarchy: in the original, titles sit close to body size (h2 24px vs 16px body, all titles underlined), so the hierarchy is flat. In the AI-built page, the featured title is about 28px bold serif and sits above smaller card titles, giving a clear scale hierarchy.

Both pages use a single red accent for category labels and buttons. The original's red is bright rgb(244,67,54) (17 backgrounds, 37 text uses). The AI-built page's red is a brick rgb(179,38,30) (3 backgrounds, 33 text uses), also used for the nav underline and header rule.

Background palette: the original has a transparent/white body with grey rgb(96,96,96) bars and translucent white strips. The AI-built page uses a warm off-white body rgb(246,244,239) with white cards, beige bands rgb(227,223,214) and deep navy rgb(20,33,61) blocks.

Top bar: both show the date. The original has a saturated blue bar rgb(30,115,190) with 'Thu. Jun 17th, 2021' in a dark grey tab above a bullet list of five categories. The AI-built page has a 40px navy strip with 'Thursday, June 17, 2021' on the left and a search form on the right.

Logo and header row: the original places a 280×165 raster swoosh logo top-left above the menu (alt 'Education Activitie'). The AI-built page uses a small 119×70 logo (alt 'Education Activities') in a header row with an empty centre, closed by a thin red rule.
The AI-built header has an italic serif quote at the right: 'Education should aim at teaching values rather than mere facts.'

Primary navigation: the original exposes an unstyled nested bullet list (Home, Certification›…, College and University›…, Education›…, Blog, Contact us) with a visible 'Primary Menu' toggle. The AI-built page has two styled nav tiers: an uppercase bold sans primary row with a red-underlined active HOME, and a grey sentence-case row of ten categories.

Primary button: the original's 'Primary Menu' button is red rgb(244,67,54) with black text, 0px radius and default 1px 6px padding. The AI-built 'Search' button is brick red with white text, 3px radius and 6px 12px padding.

Corner radius: the original is almost entirely square (1,324 elements at 0, 1 at 1–7px, none larger). The AI-built page is mostly square too (341 at 0) but has 22 elements at 1–7px (cards, input, button) and 3 at 16px or more (round avatar, pill tabs).
Both pages have minimal effects: no gradients, backdrop blur, animations or transforms. The original has 4 box-shadows and 1 transition; the AI-built page has 1 box-shadow and no transitions.
The original has broken images: carousel thumbnails and four 720×380 featured images have a 0×0 natural size and render as 19px-high alt-text links.

Top feature area: the original stacks headlines as dark text on translucent white rgba(255,255,255,0.75) strips over dark grey blocks, which reads as leftover overlay styling from missing images. The AI-built page uses a bento hero: one 680×382 featured article on the left two-thirds and three horizontal thumbnail cards stacked on the right.

Post listing layout: the original lists 300×200 thumbnails vertically, left-indented, with no grid. The AI-built page uses a four-column grid of equal-height white cards about 267px wide, each with a 166px image on top.

Content organisation: the original stacks category blocks, each headed by an h2 (College and University, Educations, Education Activities, Science, Latest Posts) with about 5 posts each. The AI-built page has one 'BROWSE ARTICLES' grid of 9 cards below the hero.
Both pages use generic stock photography for post thumbnails, such as students, campus scenes and cannabis oil/leaves, with no unified colour treatment.
The original's Science block shows large 720×380 clip-art illustrations (cartoon scientists, flasks), cropped and left-aligned.
The AI-built page scales small source images up: 300×200 files render at 680×382, and a 50×50 image renders at 265×166, which looks blurry and pixelated.

Both pages repeat the same few posts, such as '5 Big Benefits of Digital Marketing Career', 'Business English', 'masters in the Netherlands' and 'CBD'. The original repeats them across its sections; the AI-built page repeats them in both the hero and the first grid row, plus hidden 0×0 duplicate images.

Alt text: the original has 15 images with missing alt attributes out of 42, and many thumbnails have empty alt. The AI-built page has 0 missing alt attributes, but 17 of its 19 images (every card thumbnail) have empty alt.

Both pages use the same card structure: a red category link, a linked title, then a byline. On both, an excerpt appears only on a few posts; on the AI-built page only the Reddit card has a 'Summary:' paragraph.

Bylines: both credit 'WebEditor' on every post. The original uses 'By WebEditor / YYYY-MM-DD' with an underlined author link. The AI-built page uses small grey sans 'By WebEditor · May 24, 2021' with the date in a time element.

Category labels: the original has two renderings, red text on a full-width grey bar in the hero list and plain red underlined links lower down. The AI-built page uses tiny bold, uppercase, letter-spaced red sans labels, the same on all 18 cards.

The AI-built card set has inconsistencies: one 'General' card shows a letter 'G' placeholder tile instead of a photo, and one title is a bare link with no h3. The grid also ends with a single orphan card in the last row, leaving three empty columns.
The AI-built page has pill-shaped filter tabs (Latest active in red, Popular, By Category) above the grid, as button elements with no panel behaviour.
The AI-built page has a small centred red 'View all articles' button under the grid.
AI-built hero and side cards are separated from the page by a 1px border and white fill, with text placed below or beside images and never over them.

On both pages the copy reads as spun or garbled and is off-theme for education, covering CBD, treadmills and digital marketing. Both include 'No Improved Way to pick out Your Physical fitness Tools' and use inconsistent casing.

Document metadata: the original's title is 'Home - Education Activitie', with lang en-US, og/twitter meta, one JSON-LD block and a 'Skip to content' link. The AI-built page's title is 'Education Activities', with lang en, only charset/viewport/description meta and no JSON-LD.

Semantic markup: the original has header, nav, main, aside and footer, 5 sections and 0 articles, with posts built from divs and 45 figures. The AI-built page has header, 2 navs, main, 9 sections, 18 articles each with a time element, and a footer, with no aside or figure.

Code footprint: the original is heavy, with 37 scripts, 16 stylesheets, 5 style blocks, 18 inline style attributes and 1,653 class usages across 278 unique classes. The AI-built page is light, with 1 script, 1 stylesheet, 1 inline style attribute and 128 class usages across 28 unique classes. Tailwind-like utility classes are rare on both (3.6% vs 1.6%).
Link density: the original has 271 anchors and the AI-built page has 122. Each AI-built card links to the same destination three times, through the image, category and title.

Search: the original has two default-looking search forms, in the header and the footer widgets, each with a 'Search for:' label and a red button. The AI-built page has one search form, in the navy top bar.

Author info: both feature 'James E. Turner' with the same celebrity-listicle portrait (George Clooney filename). The original shows it as a widget with an h4 and a 300×173 image with no alt. The AI-built page shows a white bordered box with an 84px circular portrait (alt given), a serif name and a one-line bio.

Footer layout: the original stacks link lists vertically under h2s (Category, Quick Links, Top Category, Author Info, TAGS, Search, Latest Posts) with no background. The AI-built footer is full-bleed navy with three equal 360px columns under h4s (Quick Links, Top Categories, blurb) and near-white links.
On both pages the footer repeats header navigation: the Home/About Us/Blog/Privacy Policy/Contact us links, and a top-categories list matching five header categories.

Both footers credit the 'Daily Magazine' theme by AF themes. The original shows it as a plain left-aligned grey line with no band. The AI-built page puts a small copyright line below a thin divider on navy.
The original has a tag cloud of inline links at varying font sizes, with Education and General largest.
The original shows a partially visible reCAPTCHA-style badge fixed at the right edge, and its DOM includes an iframe and a textarea.
